federal.label: Federal: low-income housing tax credits
federal.method: Federal funding pays $443,108 of an affordable home (Exhibit F, p. 7). The Analyst says it 'includes the Low-Income Housing Tax Credit' (p. 6) and gives no split; this pool treats all of it as tax credits, which follow the project. The yearly ceiling is the most San Francisco won in one year of the award rows: 1,274 new-construction homes in 2024, times $443,108, $564,519,592 (an inference from the award records, tier 2). California sets both credits' ceilings each year: in 2026, $4.83 billion of bond ceiling for rental housing, divided among state-wide pools and six regions with no San Francisco share, and a San Francisco share of $2,861,626 a year of the 9% credit.

cite.label: Budget and Legislative Analyst, "Funding and Incentivizing Affordable Housing in San Francisco", 2026-06-05
